// Code generated by hc (handcoding). DO NOT EDIT.
//
// This file is the test driver for solution.go. It is regenerated before every
// run. ListNode and TreeNode are defined here, and so are the judge-defined
// types the problem uses (such as Node), so do not redeclare them.

package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"reflect"
	"runtime"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"sync/atomic"
	"time"
	"unicode/utf8"
)

// ListNode is a node of a singly-linked list.
type ListNode struct {
	Val  int
	Next *ListNode
}

// TreeNode is a node of a binary tree.
type TreeNode struct {
	Val   int
	Left  *TreeNode
	Right *TreeNode
}

type hcCase struct {
	ID    int                        `json:"id"`
	Input map[string]json.RawMessage `json:"input"`
}

type hcResult struct {
	ID        int             `json:"id"`
	Output    json.RawMessage `json:"output"`
	Error     string          `json:"error,omitempty"`
	ElapsedNs int64           `json:"elapsed_ns"`
	// TimeLimit marks the case hcWatch ended.
	TimeLimit bool `json:"time_limit,omitempty"`
}

type hcInputError struct{ msg string }

// The time of a case is the sum of its timed sections, the calls into the
// user's code: a class problem times each call, not the decoding of its
// arguments or the encoding of its results in between. With a time limit,
// hcWatch reads the clock while the user's code runs. A class problem's case
// can make a million calls, so hcStart and hcStop take no lock: the clock is
// two atomics, the start of the timed section (hcNotTiming between
// sections) and the time of the case's sections before it, which hcStop
// updates in that order and hcWatch reads in the other, so that it never
// counts a section twice. hcMu guards the rest: the case, the total and the
// output.
var (
	// hcBase is the origin of the clock: time.Since reads only the
	// monotonic clock.
	hcBase    = time.Now()
	hcStartNs atomic.Int64
	hcElapsed atomic.Int64
	hcMu      sync.Mutex
	// hcTotal is the time of the cases before hcCaseID, the one running.
	hcTotal  time.Duration
	hcCaseID int
	hcOut    *os.File
	hcEnc    *json.Encoder
)

const hcNotTiming = -1

func hcStart() {
	hcStartNs.Store(int64(time.Since(hcBase)))
}

func hcStop() {
	now := int64(time.Since(hcBase))
	if start := hcStartNs.Swap(hcNotTiming); start != hcNotTiming {
		hcElapsed.Add(now - start)
	}
}

// hcWatch ends the run when the time limit is spent in the middle of a
// case, which may never return, with a result line marking the case. Time
// is spent only while a section is timed, and no faster than the clock
// runs, so it sleeps for what is left of the limit.
func hcWatch(limit time.Duration) {
	for {
		hcMu.Lock()
		spent := hcTotal + time.Duration(hcElapsed.Load())
		if start := hcStartNs.Load(); start != hcNotTiming {
			spent += time.Since(hcBase) - time.Duration(start)
			if spent > limit {
				_ = hcEnc.Encode(hcResult{ID: hcCaseID, ElapsedNs: (spent - hcTotal).Nanoseconds(), TimeLimit: true})
				_ = hcOut.Sync()
				os.Exit(0)
			}
		}
		hcMu.Unlock()
		time.Sleep(max(limit-spent, time.Millisecond))
	}
}

func main() {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(os.Getenv("HC_CASES"))
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "hc driver:", err)
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	cases, n := hcParseArray(data, hcParseCase)
	if n == 0 || n != len(data) {
		cases = nil
		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &cases); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "hc driver: decode cases:", err)
			os.Exit(2)
		}
	}
	out, err := os.Create(os.Getenv("HC_OUT"))
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "hc driver:", err)
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	defer out.Close()
	enc := json.NewEncoder(out)
	enc.SetEscapeHTML(false)
	hcOut, hcEnc = out, enc
	hcStartNs.Store(hcNotTiming)
	// With a time limit, the run stops after the case whose time brings the
	// total over it.
	var limit time.Duration
	if s := os.Getenv("HC_TIME_LIMIT_NS"); s != "" {
		n, err := strconv.ParseInt(s, 10, 64)
		if err != nil || n <= 0 {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "hc driver: bad HC_TIME_LIMIT_NS:", s)
			os.Exit(2)
		}
		limit = time.Duration(n)
		go hcWatch(limit)
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		res := hcRun(c)
		hcMu.Lock()
		err := enc.Encode(res)
		_ = out.Sync()
		hcTotal += time.Duration(res.ElapsedNs)
		hcElapsed.Store(0)
		over := limit > 0 && hcTotal > limit
		hcMu.Unlock()
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "hc driver:", err)
			os.Exit(2)
		}
		if over {
			return
		}
	}
}

func hcRun(c hcCase) (res hcResult) {
	res.ID = c.ID
	defer func() {
		if r := recover(); r != nil {
			hcStop()
			res.ElapsedNs = hcElapsed.Load()
			res.Output = nil
			if ie, ok := r.(hcInputError); ok {
				res.Error = "invalid input: " + ie.msg
				return
			}
			res.Error = strings.TrimRight(fmt.Sprintf("panic: %v\n%s", r, hcStack()), "\n")
		}
	}()
	hcMu.Lock()
	hcCaseID = c.ID
	hcElapsed.Store(0)
	hcStartNs.Store(hcNotTiming)
	hcMu.Unlock()
	out, err := hcEncode(hcCall(c.Input))
	if err != nil {
		res.Error = "encode output: " + err.Error()
		return res
	}
	res.Output = out
	res.ElapsedNs = hcElapsed.Load()
	return res
}

// Outputs are encoded as encoding/json encodes them after hcNorm, with
// SetEscapeHTML(false): & < > as they are, as Python's json module writes
// them. hcAppend writes the values most outputs are made of (integers,
// booleans, plain ASCII strings and slices of them) itself, and the others
// with encoding/json, value by value: a class problem's output has a value
// per call. Should encoding/json fail on one, hcEncode encodes the output
// again as a whole, so that the error is the one it gives.
func hcEncode(v any) (json.RawMessage, error) {
	if b, ok := hcAppend(nil, v); ok {
		return b, nil
	}
	var b bytes.Buffer
	enc := json.NewEncoder(&b)
	enc.SetEscapeHTML(false)
	if err := enc.Encode(hcNorm(reflect.ValueOf(v))); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return bytes.TrimSuffix(b.Bytes(), []byte("\n")), nil
}

// hcAppend appends the JSON encoding of v to b; false when encoding/json
// fails on a value of it.
func hcAppend(b []byte, v any) ([]byte, bool) {
	switch v := v.(type) {
	case nil:
		return append(b, "null"...), true
	case int:
		return strconv.AppendInt(b, int64(v), 10), true
	case int64:
		return strconv.AppendInt(b, v, 10), true
	case bool:
		return strconv.AppendBool(b, v), true
	case string:
		return hcAppendString(b, v)
	case []any:
		return hcAppendSlice(b, v, hcAppend)
	case []int:
		return hcAppendSlice(b, v, hcAppendInt[int])
	case []int64:
		return hcAppendSlice(b, v, hcAppendInt[int64])
	case []bool:
		return hcAppendSlice(b, v, hcAppendBool)
	case []string:
		return hcAppendSlice(b, v, hcAppendString)
	case [][]int:
		return hcAppendSlice(b, v, hcAppendInts)
	}
	return hcAppendJSON(b, v)
}

func hcAppendInt[T int | int64](b []byte, n T) ([]byte, bool) {
	return strconv.AppendInt(b, int64(n), 10), true
}

func hcAppendBool(b []byte, v bool) ([]byte, bool) { return strconv.AppendBool(b, v), true }

func hcAppendInts(b []byte, s []int) ([]byte, bool) {
	return hcAppendSlice(b, s, hcAppendInt[int])
}

// hcAppendSlice writes a nil slice as [], as hcNorm has it.
func hcAppendSlice[T any](b []byte, s []T, elem func([]byte, T) ([]byte, bool)) ([]byte, bool) {
	b = append(b, '[')
	for i, x := range s {
		if i > 0 {
			b = append(b, ',')
		}
		var ok bool
		if b, ok = elem(b, x); !ok {
			return b, false
		}
	}
	return append(b, ']'), true
}

// hcAppendString writes printable ASCII without quotes and backslashes,
// which every encoder writes as it is, and leaves other strings to
// encoding/json.
func hcAppendString(b []byte, s string) ([]byte, bool) {
	for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
		if c := s[i]; c < 0x20 || c > 0x7e || c == '"' || c == '\\' {
			return hcAppendJSON(b, s)
		}
	}
	b = append(b, '"')
	b = append(b, s...)
	return append(b, '"'), true
}

var (
	hcJSONBuf bytes.Buffer
	hcJSONEnc = func() *json.Encoder {
		enc := json.NewEncoder(&hcJSONBuf)
		enc.SetEscapeHTML(false)
		return enc
	}()
)

func hcAppendJSON(b []byte, v any) ([]byte, bool) {
	hcJSONBuf.Reset()
	if err := hcJSONEnc.Encode(hcNorm(reflect.ValueOf(v))); err != nil {
		return b, false
	}
	return append(b, bytes.TrimSuffix(hcJSONBuf.Bytes(), []byte("\n"))...), true
}

// hcNorm turns nil slices into empty arrays so that a nil []int is judged
// like LeetCode does (as []), not as null.
func hcNorm(rv reflect.Value) any {
	if !rv.IsValid() {
		return nil
	}
	switch rv.Kind() {
	case reflect.Interface:
		if rv.IsNil() {
			return nil
		}
		return hcNorm(rv.Elem())
	case reflect.Slice:
		out := make([]any, rv.Len())
		for i := range out {
			out[i] = hcNorm(rv.Index(i))
		}
		return out
	}
	return rv.Interface()
}

// hcStack keeps only the frames inside the user's solution. The program is
// built with -trimpath, so the frames name solution/solution.go; the
// driver runs in the solution's directory, which gives the real path.
func hcStack() string {
	pcs := make([]uintptr, 64)
	n := runtime.Callers(3, pcs)
	frames := runtime.CallersFrames(pcs[:n])
	file := "solution.go"
	if wd, err := os.Getwd(); err == nil {
		file = wd + string(os.PathSeparator) + file
	}
	var b strings.Builder
	for {
		f, more := frames.Next()
		if strings.HasSuffix(f.File, "/solution.go") {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "    %s\n        %s:%d\n", f.Function, file, f.Line)
		}
		if !more {
			break
		}
	}
	return b.String()
}

func hcArg(in map[string]json.RawMessage, name string) json.RawMessage {
	raw, ok := in[name]
	if !ok {
		panic(hcInputError{fmt.Sprintf("missing input %q", name)})
	}
	return raw
}

func hcAt(args []json.RawMessage, i int) json.RawMessage {
	if i >= len(args) {
		panic(hcInputError{fmt.Sprintf("missing argument #%d", i)})
	}
	return args[i]
}

// hcPrefix cuts an in-place output to the length the solution returned
// (judge.output_length: return).
func hcPrefix[T any](s []T, n int) []T {
	if n < 0 || n > len(s) {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("returned length %d is outside [0, %d]", n, len(s)))
	}
	return s[:n]
}

func hcArity(op string, args []json.RawMessage, n int) {
	if len(args) != n {
		panic(hcInputError{fmt.Sprintf("%s takes %d argument(s), got %d", op, n, len(args))})
	}
}

func hcJSON[T any](raw json.RawMessage) T {
	var v T
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &v); err != nil {
		panic(hcInputError{fmt.Sprintf("decode %s as %T: %v", raw, v, err)})
	}
	return v
}

// Inputs are decoded without encoding/json where they can be: a class
// problem's case decodes every argument of every call. hc writes the cases
// as compact JSON, and the parsers below read the part of it that every
// version of encoding/json reads the same way: JSON without whitespace,
// whose strings are valid UTF-8 and escape no surrogate. A parser parses the
// value its input starts with, returning it and its length, or 0 for a
// value it does not read; encoding/json then decodes the value (or refuses
// it, with the error it gives). The parsers of values read integers,
// numbers, booleans, strings without escapes and arrays of them.

// hcDec0 decodes a value with parse.
func hcDec0[T any](raw json.RawMessage, parse func([]byte) (T, int)) T {
	if v, n := parse(raw); n > 0 && n == len(raw) {
		return v
	}
	return hcJSON[T](raw)
}

// hcDec1 decodes an array of values with parse.
func hcDec1[T any](raw json.RawMessage, parse func([]byte) (T, int)) []T {
	if v, n := hcParseArray(raw, parse); n > 0 && n == len(raw) {
		return v
	}
	return hcJSON[[]T](raw)
}

// hcDec2 decodes an array of arrays of values with parse.
func hcDec2[T any](raw json.RawMessage, parse func([]byte) (T, int)) [][]T {
	row := func(b []byte) ([]T, int) { return hcParseArray(b, parse) }
	if v, n := hcParseArray(raw, row); n > 0 && n == len(raw) {
		return v
	}
	return hcJSON[[][]T](raw)
}

// hcRaw1 splits an array into its elements.
func hcRaw1(raw json.RawMessage) []json.RawMessage {
	return hcDec1(raw, hcParseRaw)
}

// hcParseArray parses an array of values parse parses: [] is an empty
// slice, not nil, as encoding/json has it, and null is left to it.
func hcParseArray[T any](b []byte, parse func([]byte) (T, int)) ([]T, int) {
	if len(b) < 2 || b[0] != '[' {
		return nil, 0
	}
	if b[1] == ']' {
		return []T{}, 2
	}
	var out []T
	for i := 1; ; {
		v, n := parse(b[i:])
		if n == 0 {
			return nil, 0
		}
		out = append(out, v)
		i += n
		if i == len(b) {
			return nil, 0
		}
		switch b[i] {
		case ']':
			return out, i + 1
		case ',':
			i++
		default:
			return nil, 0
		}
	}
}

// hcParseCase parses a case as hc writes it, {"id":1,"input":{"name":value,
// ...}}, without a name twice.
func hcParseCase(b []byte) (hcCase, int) {
	const id, input = `{"id":`, `,"input":{`
	if !bytes.HasPrefix(b, []byte(id)) {
		return hcCase{}, 0
	}
	i := len(id)
	c := hcCase{Input: map[string]json.RawMessage{}}
	var n int
	if c.ID, n = hcParseInt(b[i:]); n == 0 || !bytes.HasPrefix(b[i+n:], []byte(input)) {
		return hcCase{}, 0
	}
	i += n + len(input)
	for i < len(b) && b[i] != '}' {
		if len(c.Input) > 0 {
			if b[i] != ',' {
				return hcCase{}, 0
			}
			i++
		}
		key, n := hcParseString(b[i:])
		if _, dup := c.Input[key]; n == 0 || dup {
			return hcCase{}, 0
		}
		i += n
		if i == len(b) || b[i] != ':' {
			return hcCase{}, 0
		}
		i++
		if n = hcSkip(b[i:]); n == 0 {
			return hcCase{}, 0
		}
		c.Input[key] = json.RawMessage(b[i : i+n])
		i += n
	}
	// The input's closing brace, then the case's.
	if i+1 >= len(b) || b[i+1] != '}' {
		return hcCase{}, 0
	}
	return c, i + 2
}

// hcSkip returns the length of the value b starts with, or 0.
func hcSkip(b []byte) int {
	if len(b) == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	switch c := b[0]; {
	case c == '"':
		return hcSkipString(b)
	case c == '[', c == '{':
		end := byte(']')
		if c == '{' {
			end = '}'
		}
		if len(b) > 1 && b[1] == end {
			return 2
		}
		for i := 1; ; {
			if c == '{' {
				n := hcSkipString(b[i:])
				if n == 0 || i+n == len(b) || b[i+n] != ':' {
					return 0
				}
				i += n + 1
			}
			n := hcSkip(b[i:])
			if n == 0 || i+n == len(b) {
				return 0
			}
			i += n
			switch b[i] {
			case end:
				return i + 1
			case ',':
				i++
			default:
				return 0
			}
		}
	case c == 't':
		if bytes.HasPrefix(b, []byte("true")) {
			return 4
		}
	case c == 'f':
		if bytes.HasPrefix(b, []byte("false")) {
			return 5
		}
	case c == 'n':
		if bytes.HasPrefix(b, []byte("null")) {
			return 4
		}
	default:
		return hcNumber(b)
	}
	return 0
}

// hcSkipString returns the length of the string b starts with, or 0: it
// takes valid UTF-8, and escapes but those of surrogates, which versions of
// encoding/json read differently.
func hcSkipString(b []byte) int {
	if len(b) == 0 || b[0] != '"' {
		return 0
	}
	for i := 1; i < len(b); {
		switch c := b[i]; {
		case c == '"':
			return i + 1
		case c < 0x20:
			return 0
		case c == '\\':
			if i+1 == len(b) {
				return 0
			}
			switch b[i+1] {
			case '"', '\\', '/', 'b', 'f', 'n', 'r', 't':
				i += 2
			case 'u':
				if i+6 > len(b) {
					return 0
				}
				r, err := strconv.ParseUint(string(b[i+2:i+6]), 16, 16)
				if err != nil || 0xd800 <= r && r <= 0xdfff {
					return 0
				}
				i += 6
			default:
				return 0
			}
		case c < utf8.RuneSelf:
			i++
		default:
			r, size := utf8.DecodeRune(b[i:])
			if r == utf8.RuneError && size == 1 {
				return 0
			}
			i += size
		}
	}
	return 0
}

// hcNumber returns the length of the number b starts with, or 0.
func hcNumber(b []byte) int {
	i := 0
	if i < len(b) && b[i] == '-' {
		i++
	}
	start := i
	for i < len(b) && '0' <= b[i] && b[i] <= '9' {
		i++
	}
	if i == start || i-start > 1 && b[start] == '0' {
		return 0
	}
	if i < len(b) && b[i] == '.' {
		i++
		start = i
		for i < len(b) && '0' <= b[i] && b[i] <= '9' {
			i++
		}
		if i == start {
			return 0
		}
	}
	if i < len(b) && (b[i] == 'e' || b[i] == 'E') {
		i++
		if i < len(b) && (b[i] == '+' || b[i] == '-') {
			i++
		}
		start = i
		for i < len(b) && '0' <= b[i] && b[i] <= '9' {
			i++
		}
		if i == start {
			return 0
		}
	}
	return i
}

// hcParseInteger parses an integer that fits in bits, without a fraction
// or an exponent, which encoding/json refuses for Go integers.
func hcParseInteger(b []byte, bits int) (int64, int) {
	n := hcNumber(b)
	digits := b[:n]
	neg := n > 0 && digits[0] == '-'
	if neg {
		digits = digits[1:]
	}
	if n == 0 || len(digits) > 18 || bits < 64 {
		// Rare: strconv tells whether it fits.
		v, err := strconv.ParseInt(string(b[:n]), 10, bits)
		if err != nil {
			return 0, 0
		}
		return v, n
	}
	var v int64
	for _, c := range digits {
		if c < '0' || c > '9' {
			return 0, 0
		}
		v = v*10 + int64(c-'0')
	}
	if neg {
		v = -v
	}
	return v, n
}

func hcParseInt(b []byte) (int, int) {
	v, n := hcParseInteger(b, strconv.IntSize)
	return int(v), n
}

func hcParseLong(b []byte) (int64, int) { return hcParseInteger(b, 64) }

func hcParseIntPtr(b []byte) (*int, int) {
	if bytes.HasPrefix(b, []byte("null")) {
		return nil, 4
	}
	v, n := hcParseInt(b)
	if n == 0 {
		return nil, 0
	}
	return &v, n
}

func hcParseDouble(b []byte) (float64, int) {
	n := hcNumber(b)
	if n == 0 {
		return 0, 0
	}
	f, err := strconv.ParseFloat(string(b[:n]), 64)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, 0
	}
	return f, n
}

func hcParseBool(b []byte) (bool, int) {
	switch {
	case bytes.HasPrefix(b, []byte("true")):
		return true, 4
	case bytes.HasPrefix(b, []byte("false")):
		return false, 5
	}
	return false, 0
}

// hcParseString parses a string without escapes.
func hcParseString(b []byte) (string, int) {
	n := hcSkipString(b)
	if n == 0 || bytes.IndexByte(b[:n], '\\') >= 0 {
		return "", 0
	}
	return string(b[1 : n-1]), n
}

// hcParseRaw takes a value as it is, as json.RawMessage does.
func hcParseRaw(b []byte) (json.RawMessage, int) {
	n := hcSkip(b)
	return json.RawMessage(b[:n]), n
}

func hcDecChar0(raw json.RawMessage) byte {
	s := hcDec0(raw, hcParseString)
	if len(s) != 1 {
		panic(hcInputError{fmt.Sprintf("character must be a 1-byte string, got %q", s)})
	}
	return s[0]
}

func hcDecChar1(raw json.RawMessage) []byte {
	parts := hcRaw1(raw)
	out := make([]byte, len(parts))
	for i, p := range parts {
		out[i] = hcDecChar0(p)
	}
	return out
}

func hcDecChar2(raw json.RawMessage) [][]byte {
	parts := hcRaw1(raw)
	out := make([][]byte, len(parts))
	for i, p := range parts {
		out[i] = hcDecChar1(p)
	}
	return out
}

func hcDecChar3(raw json.RawMessage) [][][]byte {
	parts := hcRaw1(raw)
	out := make([][][]byte, len(parts))
	for i, p := range parts {
		out[i] = hcDecChar2(p)
	}
	return out
}

func hcEncChar0(b byte) any { return string(rune(b)) }

func hcEncChar1(bs []byte) any {
	if bs == nil {
		return []string{}
	}
	out := make([]string, len(bs))
	for i, b := range bs {
		out[i] = string(rune(b))
	}
	return out
}

func hcEncChar2(bss [][]byte) any {
	out := make([]any, len(bss))
	for i, bs := range bss {
		out[i] = hcEncChar1(bs)
	}
	return out
}

func hcEncChar3(v [][][]byte) any {
	out := make([]any, len(v))
	for i, bs := range v {
		out[i] = hcEncChar2(bs)
	}
	return out
}

func hcDecList0(raw json.RawMessage) *ListNode {
	vals := hcDec1(raw, hcParseInt)
	dummy := &ListNode{}
	cur := dummy
	for _, v := range vals {
		cur.Next = &ListNode{Val: v}
		cur = cur.Next
	}
	return dummy.Next
}

func hcDecList1(raw json.RawMessage) []*ListNode {
	parts := hcRaw1(raw)
	out := make([]*ListNode, len(parts))
	for i, p := range parts {
		out[i] = hcDecList0(p)
	}
	return out
}

const hcMaxNodes = 1_000_000

func hcEncList0(head *ListNode) any {
	vals := []int{}
	for n := head; n != nil; n = n.Next {
		if len(vals) >= hcMaxNodes {
			panic("linked list too long (cycle?)")
		}
		vals = append(vals, n.Val)
	}
	return vals
}

func hcEncList1(heads []*ListNode) any {
	out := make([]any, len(heads))
	for i, h := range heads {
		out[i] = hcEncList0(h)
	}
	return out
}

func hcDecTree0(raw json.RawMessage) *TreeNode {
	vals := hcDec1(raw, hcParseIntPtr)
	if len(vals) == 0 || vals[0] == nil {
		return nil
	}
	root := &TreeNode{Val: *vals[0]}
	queue := []*TreeNode{root}
	for i := 1; i < len(vals); {
		node := queue[0]
		queue = queue[1:]
		if vals[i] != nil {
			node.Left = &TreeNode{Val: *vals[i]}
			queue = append(queue, node.Left)
		}
		i++
		if i < len(vals) && vals[i] != nil {
			node.Right = &TreeNode{Val: *vals[i]}
			queue = append(queue, node.Right)
		}
		i++
	}
	return root
}

func hcDecTree1(raw json.RawMessage) []*TreeNode {
	parts := hcRaw1(raw)
	out := make([]*TreeNode, len(parts))
	for i, p := range parts {
		out[i] = hcDecTree0(p)
	}
	return out
}

func hcEncTree0(root *TreeNode) any {
	out := []any{}
	queue := []*TreeNode{root}
	for len(queue) > 0 {
		if len(out) >= hcMaxNodes {
			panic("tree too large (cycle?)")
		}
		n := queue[0]
		queue = queue[1:]
		if n == nil {
			out = append(out, nil)
			continue
		}
		out = append(out, n.Val)
		queue = append(queue, n.Left, n.Right)
	}
	for len(out) > 0 && out[len(out)-1] == nil {
		out = out[:len(out)-1]
	}
	return out
}

func hcEncTree1(roots []*TreeNode) any {
	out := make([]any, len(roots))
	for i, r := range roots {
		out[i] = hcEncTree0(r)
	}
	return out
}

// Structure inputs (cycle, join, ref, copy, returns_ref in problem.yaml).
// A structure is handled through its nodes: a list's in order, a tree's in
// level order.

func hcListNodes(head *ListNode) []*ListNode {
	var out []*ListNode
	for n := head; n != nil; n = n.Next {
		out = append(out, n)
	}
	return out
}

func hcTreeNodes(root *TreeNode) []*TreeNode {
	var out []*TreeNode
	if root != nil {
		out = append(out, root)
	}
	for i := 0; i < len(out); i++ {
		for _, c := range []*TreeNode{out[i].Left, out[i].Right} {
			if c != nil {
				out = append(out, c)
			}
		}
	}
	return out
}

func hcHead(nodes []*ListNode) *ListNode {
	if len(nodes) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	return nodes[0]
}

// hcCycle links the tail to nodes[pos]; pos -1 means no cycle.
func hcCycle(nodes []*ListNode, pos int, name, posName string) {
	if pos < -1 || pos >= len(nodes) {
		panic(hcInputError{fmt.Sprintf("%s = %d is outside [-1, %d] for %s", posName, pos, len(nodes)-1, name)})
	}
	if pos >= 0 {
		nodes[len(nodes)-1].Next = nodes[pos]
	}
}

// hcJoin keeps the first skip nodes of b and continues with a's nodes from
// index at, returning the nodes of the joined list.
func hcJoin(b, a []*ListNode, skip, at int, bName, aName, skipName, atName string) []*ListNode {
	if skip < 0 || skip > len(b) || at < 0 || at > len(a) || len(b)-skip != len(a)-at {
		panic(hcInputError{fmt.Sprintf("%s = %d and %s = %d do not fit %s (%d nodes) and %s (%d nodes)", skipName, skip, atName, at, bName, len(b), aName, len(a))})
	}
	if skip > 0 {
		b[skip-1].Next = hcHead(a[at:])
	}
	return append(b[:skip:skip], a[at:]...)
}

func hcCopyList(head *ListNode) *ListNode {
	dummy := &ListNode{}
	for n, c := head, dummy; n != nil; n, c = n.Next, c.Next {
		c.Next = &ListNode{Val: n.Val}
	}
	return dummy.Next
}

func hcCopyTree(root *TreeNode) *TreeNode {
	if root == nil {
		return nil
	}
	return &TreeNode{Val: root.Val, Left: hcCopyTree(root.Left), Right: hcCopyTree(root.Right)}
}

func hcVal(n any) int {
	switch n := n.(type) {
	case *ListNode:
		return n.Val
	case *TreeNode:
		return n.Val
	}
	panic("hc driver: not a node")
}

// hcFind returns the node of a structure holding val, which must be unique.
func hcFind[N comparable](nodes []N, val int, name, in string) N {
	var found N
	count := 0
	for _, n := range nodes {
		if hcVal(n) == val {
			found = n
			count++
		}
	}
	switch {
	case count == 0:
		panic(hcInputError{fmt.Sprintf("%s = %d is not a value in %s", name, val, in)})
	case count > 1:
		panic(hcInputError{fmt.Sprintf("%s = %d occurs %d times in %s", name, val, count, in)})
	}
	return found
}

// hcIndex finds a returned node in its structure.
func hcIndex[N comparable](nodes []N, n N, in string) int {
	for i, x := range nodes {
		if x == n {
			return i
		}
	}
	panic(fmt.Sprintf("the returned node (Val %d) is not a node of %s", hcVal(n), in))
}

// hcListRef encodes a returned list node as its index in the list.
func hcListRef(nodes []*ListNode, n *ListNode, in string) any {
	if n == nil {
		return nil
	}
	return hcIndex(nodes, n, in)
}

// hcTreeRef encodes a returned tree node as its value.
func hcTreeRef(nodes []*TreeNode, n *TreeNode, in string) any {
	if n == nil {
		return nil
	}
	return nodes[hcIndex(nodes, n, in)].Val
}

// returns_copy: the returned structure must not share a node with the
// parameter it copies.

func hcListLinks(n *ListNode) []*ListNode { return []*ListNode{n.Next} }
func hcTreeLinks(n *TreeNode) []*TreeNode { return []*TreeNode{n.Left, n.Right} }

// hcReach collects the nodes reachable from root through links.
func hcReach[N comparable](root N, links func(N) []N) map[N]bool {
	var none N
	seen := map[N]bool{}
	stack := []N{root}
	for len(stack) > 0 {
		n := stack[len(stack)-1]
		stack = stack[:len(stack)-1]
		if n == none || seen[n] {
			continue
		}
		if len(seen) >= hcMaxNodes {
			panic("structure too large")
		}
		seen[n] = true
		stack = append(stack, links(n)...)
	}
	return seen
}

func hcCheckCopy[N comparable](orig map[N]bool, ret N, links func(N) []N, name string) {
	for n := range hcReach(ret, links) {
		if orig[n] {
			panic(fmt.Sprintf("the returned structure shares nodes with %s; return a deep copy", name))
		}
	}
}
